solves.reason: Original text: 'extensive use', 'simplifying assumptions', 'gas law is useful'. All three match choice 1.
Original: 'precisely accurate', 'meant to be descriptive', 'constraints as to how idealized'. Choice 3 matches all three.
Original: 'never entirely realized', 'make predictions', 'acceptable degrees of accuracy'. Choice 2 matches all three.
② ignore replaces 'attract'. In context, molecules 'attract or repel' each other — ignore is semantically wrong for physical force description.
③ contradictions replaces 'predictions'. Theories are used to 'make predictions' — contradictions reverses the meaning entirely.
④ valuable replaces 'worthless'. Original says they cannot be so far removed as to be 'worthless' — valuable is the exact opposite.
The passage topic is idealizations in science. 'The sciences do make extensive use of ____.' = idealizations. The word 'idealized' later confirms this theme.
'There are, accordingly, ____ as to how idealized they can be.' Only constraints fits as a limitation on degree of idealization.
'the theories are still meant to be ____.' Followed by 'used to make predictions and offer explanations' — descriptive is the purpose.
extensive = widespread (broad/wide-ranging). intensive means deep/concentrated, which is the opposite dimension.
obtain here = prevail/hold true (formal usage). 'conditions that never perfectly obtain' = conditions that never fully come into effect.
regarded = considered. 'best regarded as models' = best considered as models.
simplifying ↔ elaborating. Elaborating means adding complexity/detail, the opposite of simplifying. Clarifying/reducing are aligned with simplifying.
worthless ↔ invaluable. Invaluable = beyond value, priceless. Despite the 'in-' prefix, it means extremely valuable, not valueless.
(A) 'at issue' = matter/question being discussed (noun). (B) 'issue a statement' = publish/release (verb). Different parts of speech and meanings.
'a limitation or restriction on what can be done' = constraint. Matches perfectly with the passage usage of constraints on idealization.
real → realized. 'conditions that are never entirely ____ (real)' — be + past participle passive form. Realized = brought into actuality.
describe → descriptive. 'meant to be ____' requires adjective complement. Descriptive = having the quality of describing.
'their behavior is nonetheless ____' — despite being different, real gas behavior is 'close enough to ideal ones that the gas law is useful'. 'nonetheless' signals this concession.
'They cannot be ____ with acceptable degrees of accuracy.' = 'so far removed from real world systems as to be worthless'. The structure 'cannot be so X as to be Y' fits.
